title: I Gave an AI Engineer Access to My Whole Business
lesson: Persistent business context plus a concrete request can produce a relevant deliverable; a strong edit connects the source information, constraints and visible result, then explains the resulting workflow benefit.
opening: The hook names a high-stakes existing object—one repository for the creator’s business—and asks what happens when Devin gets access. A red arrow/repository view and working-person cut make the object and owner concrete before the agent is named.
story_arc: Establish business repo → name agent and environment → montage claimed indexing/wiki artifacts → reset to one concrete waitlist request → show program and brand sources → show matching page → spotlight result → introduce Slack participation and conceptual parallelism → return to repository as the reason repeated explanation is avoided → preview setup resource.
payoff: The concrete waitlist page visibly answers the request and reflects the supplied branding. Several intervening images illustrate categories rather than proving the exact claims: planner for browser, code diff for wiki, generic graph/document for repo knowledge, and a website form for pull request.
selection_reason: A complete task-to-result story with real constraint artifacts, reusable split layout, two distinct attention spotlights, an opening-object callback and tangible CTA preview. Its mismatched filler images and decorative parallel-worker close view show what a directing library should flag rather than imitate.
review_limits: Viewed all 4 chronological 0.5-second context pages (70 samples including final frame) plus 69 framing samples on 8 extra strips. Original machine-caption grouping supplies spoken ideas; no audio audition or phonetic verification. Caption final word overruns video; source was not padded or retimed. Strip timestamps are ffmpeg eight-fps resampling estimates, not source-frame measurements. Continuous motion, exact typography, easing, generation provenance and product claims are not independently verified. Catalog source inspection supports possible mechanisms only; no rendered match or ready replica is claimed.
